albums.blurb: Fukui was a self-taught pianist from Hokkaido who later ran Sapporo's Slowboat jazz club with his wife; Scenery was his 1976 debut, a trio session that pairs standards like "Autumn Leaves," "Willow Weep for Me," and "It Could Happen to You" with originals including the driving "Early Summer," in a modal, hard-swinging style often compared to McCoy Tyner and Bill Evans. Every track is instrumental piano-trio jazz.
albums.reception: Virtually unnoticed outside Japan on release, the album became a cult classic decades later, and reissue label We Release Jazz has called it "unquestionably one of the most important Japanese jazz albums ever recorded."

albums.blurb: Badu's second studio album and the follow-up to Baduizm, cut at Electric Lady Studios with the Soulquarians collective — Questlove on drums, James Poyser on keys, Pino Palladino on bass, J Dilla among the producers — plus trumpeter Roy Hargrove. It traded her debut's polish for looser live instrumentation and yielded "Bag Lady," her first top-ten single on the Billboard Hot 100.
albums.reception: Mama's Gun peaked at No. 11 on the Billboard 200, was certified platinum by the RIAA within a month of release, and was ranked the ninth-best album of 2000 by Rolling Stone.

albums.blurb: Stereolab are an Anglo-French group built around guitarist Tim Gane and singer Lætitia Sadier, who folds French- and English-language vocals into motorik krautrock grooves, '60s French pop, lounge, and analog electronics. Emperor Tomato Ketchup, their fourth album, is the loop-driven record generally treated as the definitive entry point to their catalog.
albums.reception: Pitchfork placed it 51st on its list of the top 100 albums of the 1990s, calling it the band's "most definitive and recommended statement," and it is included in 1001 Albums You Must Hear Before You Die.
